display.purpose: Chapter titles, the shelf heading, the name on a cover, the date on a milestone card.

headline.purpose: The parents' desk heading and walkthrough step titles.

title.purpose: Handwritten lines under a display heading: month range, shelf line, nameplate.

hand.purpose: Print captions, milestone titles, note slips, cassette labels.

body.purpose: Desk copy, reader story text, form values.

label.purpose: Field labels, index tabs, corner links; buttons use the same weight at 1rem.

shadows.name: print
shadows.purpose: Anything lying on a sheet: prints, date cards, note slips, cassettes, desktop index tabs.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Something picked up: the print in the reader, the page block under a shelf book.

shadows.name: sticker
shadows.purpose: Filter shadow following a sticker's die-cut outline.

shadows.name: cover-board
shadows.purpose: The swinging cover over the page beneath.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Shared default: how things settle onto a page. Entries stagger 70ms across a row.

motion.name: slap
motion.purpose: Stickers landing, 250 to 350ms after their entry.

motion.name: shelf
motion.purpose: Books arriving on the shelf, 80ms apart.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Button press and hover scale (150 to 200ms), tape press (220ms), walkthrough page slide (260ms), tab slide (300ms).

motion.name: cover-open
motion.purpose: Button-driven scroll that swings the cover from 0 to -96deg on its spine; otherwise scroll-linked.

motion.name: reel
motion.purpose: Cassette reels while a song plays; motion-safe only.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Everything rests in place; the cover is a static first screen.

narrative.overview:
The browser window is a cloth-bound baby journal. A journal's first screen is its closed cover in the child's colour; scrolling swings that cover open on its spine, and everything after is sheets of coloured sugar paper, one per age, with prints taped down by hand. Every surface is a named material: bookcloth, sugar paper, white print stock, washi tape, die-cut sticker vinyl, ruled note paper, an endpaper of dots, a navy album page of cassettes. All of it is drawn in code. The textures are procedural SVG noise and gradients, and the only rasters are the family's own photographs.

The mood is loud, warm and handmade: saturated colour at full bleed, chunky stamped lettering, handwriting wherever the book is written in, and nothing lined up quite straight. Density is low. A sheet holds a handful of things with generous paper around them, and a sheet with only one or two entries gives them more room and alternates sides, the way a hand-filled album does.

Motion follows one grammar: things are placed, not faded. Prints arrive a little high and turned, then settle on a spring; tape presses down after them; stickers are slapped on with a bounce; opening a print lifts that same print off the page into the reader. The parents' desk is the same world at lower volume: plain paper, navy ink, pill controls, and a live preview of the entry on the sheet it will land on.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed coloured surfaces; no neutral page chrome anywhere in the reading experience.
Three typefaces with fixed jobs: stamped display, handwriting, and a plain grotesk for controls.
Navy ink for all text, borders and shadows. There is no grey and no black.
Deterministic hand-placement: each entry's tilt, nudge, tape side and tape colour are seeded from its id, so the page looks arranged by hand and renders identically every time.
Pills for anything pressed; near-square corners for anything made of paper.

rules.name: The Navy Ink Rule
rules.body: Text, outlines and shadows are navy (`ink`), at full strength or as a transparency of it. Grey and black do not appear.

rules.name: The Paired Foreground Rule
rules.body: A cloth or tone never sets its own text colour. It carries a foreground with it: cream on tomato, cobalt, leaf and plum; ink on marigold. Ink on those four saturated cloths fails contrast (below 3:1), and cream on marigold fails worse (1.9:1).

rules.name: The Soft Ink Stays on Paper Rule
rules.body: `ink-soft` is for paper and the lilac wash. On rose and lilac sheets it drops to about 4.4:1, so text on sugar paper is full ink.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Caprasimo is stamped or printed on the book. Gochi Hand is written in the book by a person: captions, firsts, notes, inscriptions. Schibsted Grotesk is the app speaking: controls, hints, system copy. A control is never set in the hand, and a caption is never set in the grotesk.

rules.name: The Ruled Line Rule
rules.body: Handwriting on ruled paper locks to the 1.75rem rule: line-height, the gap before the sign-off and the top offset are all multiples of it.

rules.name: The Lying Flat Rule
rules.body: A shadow says how far a thing is off the paper. Resting things take the print shadow, held things the lifted one. Shadows are never decoration and never coloured anything but ink.

rules.name: The Placed, Not Faded Rule
rules.body: Entrances are physical. An entry arrives 30px high, 5 degrees over-turned and 6% large, then settles on the shared spring (stiffness 300, damping 26, mass 0.9), staggered 70ms across a row. Tape presses on 280ms later, scaling down from 150%. Stickers land last on a bouncier spring (stiffness 420, damping 16). Only transform and opacity animate. With reduced motion, or before the animation engine loads, everything rests in place and the cover becomes a static first screen.

dos: Do set every piece of text in `ink`, or in the foreground paired with its cloth: cream on tomato, cobalt, leaf and plum, ink on marigold.
Do give each chapter the next sheet in the order sky, butter, rose, mint, lilac, and cut it from the one above with the pinked edge.
Do tilt anything lying on a sheet between 1.2 and 3.6 degrees, seeded from its id so server and client agree.
Do tape photos, videos and notes down with one washi strip in a tone colour. Date cards are not taped.
Do keep hit areas at 2.75rem or more and every pressed control a pill or a circle.
Do bring things in by placing them: transform and opacity only, on the shared settle spring, once per element.
Do show a parent the entry on its real sheet colour before they add it.
Do build new materials procedurally (SVG filters, gradients, masks). The only rasters are photographs.
Do honour reduced motion with a fully laid-out, still page.
donts: Don't use grey or black for text, borders or shadows. Use ink or a transparency of it.
Don't lay entries out as an equal-card photo grid. Spans follow what the entry is and how full the sheet is.
Don't put the whole product on cream paper. Paper is for prints, slips and the desk; the journal's pages are coloured.
Don't set controls or system copy in Gochi Hand, or captions and notes in Schibsted Grotesk.
Don't add a dark theme, glows, blurs or gradient fills. Colour is flat and depth is a short navy shadow.
Don't let parents choose stickers. They are dealt by the book.
